title: Social Post: Ghost Drone at Birch Hollow Range

fields.imageBrief: drone-like object hovering over a wooden lodge roof, sunlight glinting off plastic casing, ground-level photo taken through a window
fields.caption: UAS-11 just flew over the lodge patio and dropped a fake drone on the roof. It’s not a real drone, right? #BirchHollowIncident #GhostDrone

comments.text: That’s not a UAS. That’s a toy. Did they really send a drone to drop a prop?
This is going viral. The fake drone is clearly not a real aircraft. Why would they do that?

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance at an open grass flight test field: a multirotor drone on a landing pad, a crew in high-visibility vests at a folding table, orange cones, a windsock, clear sky. Phone snapshot taken from inside a base building window, low angle toward the roof of a wooden lodge in a wooded preserve. A drone-like object with a plastic casing and visible propeller blades hovers just above the roofline, sunlight glinting off its smooth surface. The background shows tree branches and a partial view of a base walkway. The photo is slightly tilted, with a flash bloom on the right edge, and the lens shows a soft blur on the distant trees. The window is unobstructed, no visible glass reflections. The sky is clear and bright, midday. No people visible, only the object and the roof.
